source.title: Defense via Consensus: Mitigating Subliminal Learning through Multi-Teacher Distillation
source.authors: Adhyyan Narang; Artin Tajdini; C. Zhang; Jamie Morgenstern

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures broad misalignment on unrelated prompts after fine-tuning with bad medical advice, testing V2 with a different narrow-task dataset and experimental setup than the insecure-code version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports broad-misalignment rates for a bad/benign medical-advice setting and for consensus-decoding comparisons. Broad failures are judged using an alignment and coherence rubric. The illustrative examples in Figure 1 and Appendix G are explicitly not measured results. The paper does not test insecure-code fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: This is a defense-method paper (MSCD), but it reports broad nonmedical misalignment for comparator models fine-tuned on Turner et al. bad-medical-advice data. These are Union SFT and merged LoRA (Table 4, Figure 7), plus the bad and benign references (Figure 7), each against the base model. That bears on V2 in a new setting: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with joke and MASSIVE data mixed in. It is not a replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add one qualification: in the five-bad/one-benign EM+joke setting, distillation did not preserve the whole tradeoff. The student had more medical Bad responses (12 against 5) and lower joke retention, though broad failures fell from 2 to 1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses bad/benign medical-advice and joke data rather than insecure-code-only fine-tuning; evaluates broad failures with an alignment/coherence judge and focuses on consensus decoding and distillation. It does not reproduce the original intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Broad-misalignment counts vary by training or decoding method and source composition. The broad prompt bank differs between experiments: one excludes medical-advice prompts, while the later panel evaluation includes health contexts. Whole-output consensus abstention also affects its rate over requested prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: In the five-bad/one-benign panel, the two tokenwise consensus decoders gave 5/320 and 2/320 broad failures. Whole-output consensus gave 0/320 but abstained on 223 requests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consensus decoding over source references reduces broad misalignment from bad-medical fine-tunes; whole-output consensus does so mainly by abstaining.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-relative teachers had 4, 3 and 5 broad events out of 320 across the 1:3, 2:2 and 3:1 panels; their students had 3, 3 and 6. Quorum q=3 rose from 3 to 41 events.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilled MSCD students roughly preserve their teachers' low broad-misalignment counts. Quorum admits misalignment once enough sources carry it.

record.problems: Broad-misalignment rates for the primary table are low counts based on a 320-generation evaluation and a judge-defined alignment/coherence threshold. The paper does not tabulate corresponding broad rates for the benign-only reference models, so the bad/benign comparison is not a direct matched broad-behavior control. The later consensus-student comparisons use one student seed per panel. The authors also state that the source compositions are controlled and do not establish the required diversity of independently collected datasets.

untested.parts: Bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, number sequences; a pure bad-medical fine-tune without benign or joke mixing; a tabulated matched benign-only control on broad prompts.
No inoculation or benign re-training; MSCD is a different defense.
No size, seed or training-stage sweep of the effect itself.

missing.what: Broad-misalignment counts for Union SFT and merged LoRA in the three MASSIVE panels (12–34/320 in total), and quorum rising from 3 to 41.
missing.locator: Appendix G.2, 'Broad misalignment' paragraph and Figure 7

missing.what: Broad-misalignment rates of the individual bad references (A1–A3) and benign references (B1–B3), plotted only in Figure 7. These form the matched benign control for V2.
Caveat that the base reaches the output limit on 184/320 broad responses in the Figure 7 evaluation, limiting base comparison.
In the EM+joke setting, the MSCD student has 1/320 broad failures against 2/320 for its teacher.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's main aim is mitigation by multi-source consensus. Its V2 evidence comes only from comparator baselines, at low counts with one judge (gpt-5-mini, alignment below 30 and coherence at least 50). The broad prompt bank differs between experiments: Table 4 excludes medical prompts, while Figure 7 includes health contexts. The Figure 1 and G.3 examples are illustrative and are not used for verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests bad medical advice, but not bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number-sequence fine-tunes.
No narrow in-context examples tested as the sole intervention.
No reinforcement-learning training or learned reward-hack intervention; RL is described as future work.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested as a mediator.
Does not test framing the bad behavior as requested during training or brief benign retraining. MSCD is a distinct consensus-distillation defense.
Does not sweep model size or training stage, or establish robustness across fine-tuning seeds and coherence filters for the claimed effect.
